siblings.summary: Where to eat your way through Singapore's hawker legends, crab feasts, Peranakan-Indian-Malay-Chinese threads, and offbeat supper spots on a first visit.

siblings.title: Sleep — Singapore: Character Stays for a First Visit
siblings.summary: Character over category: shophouse, design, heritage and treehouse stays across Singapore's six base neighbourhoods, plus the one first-visit icon.

siblings.title: Do — Singapore: semi-adventurous activities for a first visit
siblings.summary: Trek-light, kayak, cycle, swim and snorkel-light dos around Singapore — difficulty, guide-need and half/full-day for each.

siblings.title: See — Singapore: the unmissable icons + heritage to see (first-visit guide)
siblings.summary: The can't-miss Singapore icons, ethnic-quarter heritage, UNESCO Botanic Gardens, and offbeat sights — ranked must-do vs skippable.

siblings.title: Offbeat Singapore: The Weird Stuff a First-Timer Misses
siblings.summary: A themed field guide to Singapore's strangest corners — hells, ghost reservoirs, last villages, leaning mosques and dragon kilns.

siblings.title: Around & day-trips — Singapore (first-visit guide)
siblings.summary: Changi-to-city options, getting around by MRT/Grab, and the day-trip orbit (Pulau Ubin, southern islands, Johor Bahru, Bintan).

sources.title: Singapore Art Week (SAW) returns from 22 to 31 January 2026 for its 14th edition, with more than 100 exhibitions, events, and programmes.
sources.claim: Singapore Art Week 2026 runs 22-31 Jan, its 14th edition, with 100+ exhibitions citywide as SE Asia's pinnacle visual-arts season.

sources.title: In 2026 (Year of the Horse), Chinese New Year falls on 17-18 February.
sources.claim: Chinese New Year 2026 (Year of the Horse) falls 17-18 February, with Chinatown light-up and River Hongbao.

sources.title: The Singapore Grand Prix is scheduled to take place on the weekend of 9-11 October.
sources.claim: The Singapore Grand Prix night street race is held 9-11 October 2026 at the Marina Bay circuit.

sources.title: Thaipusam is happening on 1 February 2026. The procession begins on 31 January 2026 at 11.30pm.
sources.claim: Thaipusam 2026 is on 1 February with the kavadi procession beginning the night of 31 January; not a public holiday.

sources.title: Chingay 2026 will take place on 27 and 28 February 2026 from 8pm to 9:30pm at the F1 Pit Building.
sources.claim: Chingay Parade 2026 takes place 27-28 February at the F1 Pit Building, Singapore's largest multicultural street parade.

sources.title: The 2026 edition runs from 18 September to 20 October 2026, with the free street light-up illuminating Chinatown.
sources.claim: Mid-Autumn 2026 falls ~25 Sep; Chinatown's street light-up runs 18 Sep-20 Oct nightly.

sources.title: Hari Raya Puasa - Saturday, 21 March; Vesak Day - Sunday, 31 May; Hari Raya Haji - Wednesday, 27 May; National Day - Sunday, 9 August; Deepavali - Sunday, 8 November.
sources.claim: Official 2026 Singapore public holidays: CNY 17-18 Feb, Hari Raya Puasa 21 Mar, Vesak 31 May, Hari Raya Haji 27 May, National Day 9 Aug, Deepavali 8 Nov.

sources.title: Deepavali ... is celebrated in Little India with beautiful light displays and street decorations.
sources.claim: Deepavali (8 Nov 2026 public holiday) is celebrated in Little India with light displays, night markets and bazaars.

sources.title: From 13 - 17 January 2026, Little India will bustle with even more colour and life than usual for the 2026 Pongal Festival.
sources.claim: Pongal 2026, the Tamil harvest festival, runs 13-17 January in Little India.

sources.title: Fire Walking 2025 - Sri Mariamman Temple - HEB
sources.claim: The Theemithi firewalking ceremony is organised by the Hindu Endowments Board at Sri Mariamman Temple.

sources.title: Thaipusam
sources.claim: Thaipusam commemorates devotees fulfilling vows; the procession runs to Sri Thendayuthapani Temple on Tank Road.

sources.title: Indian Heritage Centre - Pongal 2026 Open House
sources.claim: The Indian Heritage Centre (Little India) runs an annual Pongal Open House (10, 11, 17, 18 Jan 2026).

sources.title: The Hungry Ghost Festival 2026 officially starts on 13 August 2026, with Ghost Day taking place on 27 August 2026.
sources.claim: The Hungry Ghost Festival 2026 spans the 7th lunar month, 13 Aug-11 Sep, with Ghost Day on 27 August.

sources.title: Geylang becomes one of the most popular spots, being the host to the largest Getai performances during the Hungry Ghost month.
sources.claim: Getai are loud Hokkien-dialect variety concerts staged for spirits in the 7th month, with Geylang and heartland estates the authentic venues.

sources.title: Theemithi
sources.claim: Theemithi is a Hindu firewalking rite held about a week before Deepavali (Tamil month of Aipasi, Oct-Nov) at Sri Mariamman Temple.

sources.title: Singapore's National Day Parade is set to make a long-awaited return to the National Stadium for the first time since 2016.
sources.claim: National Day Parade 2026 returns to the National Stadium (~42,000 capacity) on 9 August with the theme Majulah Singapura, Go Beyond!

sources.title: Tickets | National Day Parade 2026
sources.claim: NDP 2026 tickets are balloted via Singpass for Singapore citizens and PRs only (applications 23 May-6 Jun 2026).

sources.title: 38 Unique and Cool Creative Workshops in Singapore
sources.claim: Singapore offers many short creative workshops including pottery hand-building, calligraphy and heritage crafts.

sources.title: The Singapore Night Festival welcomes everyone to enjoy 16 nights of installations and creative encounters from August until Sep 2026 in Bras Basah.Bugis.
sources.claim: Singapore Night Festival runs across late Aug to early Sep with free night-time light installations in the Bras Basah.Bugis arts district.

sources.title: Light to Night Singapore 2026 celebrates its 10th edition from 9-31 January.
sources.claim: Light to Night Singapore 2026 (10th edition) runs 9-31 January with facade projections and installations across the Civic District.

sources.title: Festival Dates: February 27 - March 8, 2026 ... Free Outdoor Performances ... at the DBS Foundation Outdoor Theatre.
sources.claim: Huayi - Chinese Festival of Arts 2026 runs 27 Feb-8 Mar at Esplanade with free outdoor performances and crafts plus ticketed theatre and orchestra shows.

sources.title: A lion dance will be performed by the award-winning Yi Wei Athletic Association (Singapore) on Huayi's opening day.
sources.claim: Huayi 2026 opens with an award-winning lion dance and includes Fujian opera demos and a Singapore Chinese Orchestra Monkey King puppetry concert.

sources.title: Singapore's oldest museum features a blend of colonial architecture and modern design ... galleries like the Singapore History Gallery.
sources.claim: The National Museum of Singapore is the country's oldest, blending colonial architecture with an immersive Singapore History Gallery.

sources.title: teamLab Future World, ArtScience Museum, Marina Bay Sands, Singapore
sources.claim: The ArtScience Museum hosts teamLab Future World, a permanent interactive digital-art exhibition.

sources.title: Selected areas will be temporarily unavailable from 15 Jun to 28 Aug 2026 as enhancements take place.
sources.claim: Selected Future World areas at the ArtScience Museum are temporarily unavailable 15 Jun-28 Aug 2026 for enhancements.

sources.title: ACM's 13 permanent galleries highlight cross-cultural flows ... the newly refreshed Scholars Gallery.
sources.claim: The Asian Civilisations Museum (Empress Place) has 13 galleries on Asia's cross-cultural trade flows, including a refreshed Scholars Gallery.

sources.title: Peranakan Museum
sources.claim: The Peranakan Museum at 39 Armenian Street reopened after a major revamp with nine galleries of Straits-Chinese material culture.

sources.title: The museum features nine galleries spread across three floors, with over 800 artifacts.
sources.claim: The reopened Peranakan Museum features nine galleries across three floors with over 800 artifacts.

sources.title: NUS Baba House - A Straits Chinese heritage property, featuring a collection of unique artifacts.
sources.claim: NUS Baba House is a restored Straits-Chinese ancestral home on Neil Road, visitable by guided appointment only.

sources.title: This museum houses over 50,000 toys from 40 countries, spanning most of the 20th century.
sources.claim: The Mint Museum of Toys holds 50,000+ toys from 40 countries; other quirky options include the Live Turtle & Tortoise Museum and Katong Antique House.

sources.title: The-Intan | My Rose Cut Diamond - An award winning Peranakan home museum
sources.claim: The Intan is an award-winning private Peranakan home-museum in Joo Chiat, visitable by appointment.

sources.title: The museum contains over 5,000 Peranakan objects ... Visits to The Intan are strictly by appointments only.
sources.claim: The Intan holds over 5,000 Peranakan objects and offers personal tours with tea, strictly by appointment.

sources.title: Hell's Museum - Haw Par Villa
sources.claim: Hell's Museum at Haw Par Villa centres on the Ten Courts of Hell and is billed the world's first museum on death and the afterlife.

sources.title: Haw Par Villa is partially closed from 8 December 2025 until further notice, though Hell's Museum featuring the Ten Courts of Hell remains open.
sources.claim: Haw Par Villa is an 8.5-ha cultural park (built 1937 by the Tiger Balm magnate); the wider park is partially closed from 8 Dec 2025 while Hell's Museum stays open.

sources.title: The Malay Heritage Centre ... houses the Istana Kampong Gelam ... Sun Yat Sen Nanyang Memorial Hall.
sources.claim: Community heritage venues include the Malay Heritage Centre (Istana Kampong Gelam) and Sun Yat Sen Nanyang Memorial Hall.

sources.title: Cultural Workshops - batik, Peranakan beading, calligraphy, pottery - normally $60-120.
sources.claim: Heritage-craft workshops (batik, Peranakan beading, calligraphy, pottery) typically cost about S$60-120.

sources.title: Singapore Musical Box Museum ... Fuk Tak Chi Museum ... Lee Kong Chian Natural History Museum.
sources.claim: Small offbeat museums include the Singapore Musical Box Museum (Boat Quay), Fuk Tak Chi temple-museum (1824) and Lee Kong Chian Natural History Museum.

sources.title: What's On at Esplanade Singapore | Free Performances Every Day
sources.claim: Esplanade - Theatres on the Bay stages free performances every day on its concourse and outdoor venues.

sources.title: Wayang, Chinese Street Opera, Stages a Comeback in Singapore
sources.claim: Wayang (Chinese street opera), once declining, is seeing a revival in Singapore.

sources.title: Wayang (Chinese Street Opera) - Singapore
sources.claim: Wayang is face-painted, gong-driven Chinese street opera traditionally staged on makeshift platforms at temple festivals.

sources.title: Tekka Centre is part wet market, part hawker centre ... Chinatown Street Market is famous for its colorful stalls.
sources.claim: Tekka Centre mixes wet market, hawker centre and tailors; Chinatown Street Market sells souvenirs and festive goods.

sources.title: MAAD stands for Market of Artists And Designers and is held one Friday night each month at the Red Dot Design Museum.
sources.claim: MAAD (Market of Artists And Designers) is a monthly Friday-night indie design/craft market at Red Dot Design Museum.

sources.title: 2026 guide to Singapore flea markets & fairs: Best pop-ups, boutiques and places to pick up unique finds.
sources.claim: Singapore hosts rotating weekend flea and maker pop-ups for vintage, handmade and sustainable goods.

sources.title: Kamal Arts, Singapore - Artists - Gallery - Batik Painting Workshop in Singapore
sources.claim: Kamal Arts (Geylang Serai) runs batik painting workshops teaching traditional waxing and dyeing of the regional textile craft.

sources.title: The workshop typically runs for an hour, with a cost of S$88.
sources.claim: Oo La Lab (71 Amoy St, Chinatown) runs ~1-hour perfume-making workshops for about S$88 to bottle your own scent.

sources.title: Perfume Creation masterclass in Singapore
sources.claim: Maison 21G offers bespoke perfume-creation masterclasses where guests take home a 30ml Eau de Parfum.

sources.title: Colourfully Peranakan - Beading Workshop
sources.claim: Peranakan beading workshops let participants string Miyuki-bead jewellery on heritage motifs at the Singapore Chinese Cultural Centre.
